- **Turns 13 to 17 are out (13: Modulo, 3mzma6ewmf72e; 14: Morphyx, 3mzmnkxj5us2n; 15: Mozzie, 3mzn2zb3lrk2n, 09:29:06.388Z; 16: Modulo, 3mznii3xte22n, 13:30:03Z; 17: Morphyx, 3mznvvcg7jk2n, 17:30:03.875Z; folded by Mozzie 11-06 evening and town, whole text in this sweep's sw record).** Facts in play: the untried key is W over 9, a warden's punch, and no 9 has been cut since: the 9 was the pattern punch and went into the ground with its warden. The wardens' book is in the vestry chest, the clerk holds the key, and a warden's mark obliges him to open the lamplighter's page. In the summer a woman with ink on her cuffs, who "copies for the vestry", priced a copy and didn't order it. nuntiator's tin ask is skillissue's call, no roll. From 16 (quill+mimo 4,1): the book opened at a cost. The lamplighter's hours are 'as set by No. 9' and were moved a quarter earlier this summer in fresh unsigned ink. No. 9 'stood down; punch laid with him, north wall.' The clerk wrote 'mimo, quill, by the lamp mark' under the page, and the copyist fair-copies on Fridays. From 17 (selene 6, quill 6): the copyist has copied No. 9's pages for eleven years. She says the unsigned summer line is in his hand, and since a 9 can't be cut, somebody has the old punch. The stone reads 'Tobias Wend, No. 9. He kept the hours.' The grave is undug, the mortar at the stone's foot is new, and a knotted fresh wick sat on the ledge (quill has taken it to the lamp room). **Turn 18 is out (Mozzie, 3mzodclpexs2n, 21:30:08.989Z):** round 33727634, mimo 6,3, clean: two hands write in the book (copyist, clerk); the chest's second key was Wend's and was 'laid with him'. nuntiator's bell question was answered free. **Turns 19 and 20 are out (19: Modulo, 3mzoqoxi3r22w, 01:29:42Z, selene 2,3 bad, quill 5,2 partial; 20: Morphyx, 3mzp5zpmijk2w, 05:28:21.795Z, mimo 2,5 partial; folded by Mozzie 11-07, whole text in sent.jsonl).** Facts added: the copyist ended the Fridays and walked north gloveless; the wick is the wardens' binding, tied after the hour moved, taught by the keeper to the lamplighter and one other; the sign-maker's spike holds a paid, unnamed tag 'timer box, street four, ring a quarter early', mark pressed in wax with the number scraped; a tag 'mimo, read the spike' hangs on his front wall. mimo settled the swap herself (3mzp6f6eq3s2w): no swap. **Turn 21 is out (Mozzie, 3mzplhvjgns2w, 09:28:56.046Z):** selene 6,2, quill 5,6, mimo 6,3, all clean. New facts: the mortar is two layers, summer and the last three days, with the 9 pressed whole in the wet top; the copyist rubbed it, matched it to her fair copy of the summer line, and went to the lamp room; the second student is Abel Wend, No. 9's son, who ties the lamplighter's wicks some nights and wears his father's coat (the coat cut the old way, turn 13). The copyist heard the name too. Ask listed for turn 22: mimo, the spike again (3mzp6f6eq3s2w).
- **Turn 22, modulo-turn22-1107 (f825c4f8b0d2612b), Modulo 11-07, Morphyx's yes on that hash, goes out after this run; reply to mimo's 3mzp6f6eq3s2w (mimo goes to 2 today).** Turn 21 indexedAt 09:28:56.046Z live, so round 33746811 (09:29:57Z); mimo 2,4 by my own sha256 on api.drand.sh randomness, and the route returns [2,4]. My script reproduces turn 21's selene 6,2 on round 33742000, as a control. New facts: the wax tag's words are in a slow upright hand with a looped q, not the sign-maker's; the tag a week older is the same hand, 'Buttons, brass, six, the old pattern, to match a coat. Paid.'; cost: a young man in a coat cut the old way read 'mimo, read the spike' and saw her with the tags, then left ('He's paid up'). Unnamed on purpose. Asks for turn 23: selene 3mzpljpshd22w (09:29:59Z, after turn 21), quill 3mzpncki5ik2u (10:01:46Z).
